name: Highlands 40

nadir.desc: The nadir view shows a single-story tan/stucco residence with a multi-section roof plan, solar panels visible on the roof, and a detached structure or garage positioned to the northwest of the main residence|A paved driveway loops from the street connection point, curves through the property, and provides a turning area near the structures|A rectangular light-colored feature, consistent with a swimming pool or spa, is visible on the south side of the residence adjacent to a small area of green lawn|The surrounding parcel is desert scrubland with scattered juniper trees and no visible perimeter fencing, and the property is accessed via a curved paved driveway connecting to what appears to be Macalpine Loop to the east.

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front of the residence from the street side, revealing a low-profile single-story structure with a flat-to-low-pitch roof composed of multiple connected sections|The paved driveway curves from the front of the property through sparse desert scrub and juniper vegetation before reaching the building cluster|No visible perimeter fencing or gate structures are present along the front access route|The road bordering the front of the property runs along the right edge of this view.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the property from the right side, revealing the driveway curving in from the upper right and terminating in a paved area adjacent to the main structures|Solar panels are visible on the roof section of the main residence|A small green lawn area and the light-colored pool or spa structure are visible on the near side of the residence|Multiple juniper trees are distributed around the structure with no fencing observed on this side.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the residence with the main structure and its connected or closely positioned secondary structure visible together|The green lawn area and rectangular light-colored pool or spa are visible directly behind the main building|Desert scrub and juniper trees surround the rear and sides of the structure with no fencing or walls observed|A road is visible along the upper left edge of this view, confirming road access on at least two sides of the parcel.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property with the residence positioned in the upper center of the frame and a paved road running along the lower left|The building mass appears as a compact cluster of connected single-story sections|No fencing, outbuildings, or secondary structures are visible on this side|The terrain between the road and the structures is open desert scrub with scattered junipers, offering clear sightlines to the building.

considerations: The property is accessed by a single paved driveway that loops from Macalpine Loop, providing a turning area near the structures suitable for emergency vehicles. The surrounding terrain is open desert scrub with no perimeter fencing observed, allowing foot access from multiple directions. Solar panels are present on the roof and should be noted for responder awareness during roof operations. Scattered juniper trees throughout the parcel are the primary vegetation in proximity to the structures and should be noted relative to fire behavior in the area.
clarifications: Is there a gate or any access control at the driveway entrance from Macalpine Loop? Does the driveway surface support the weight of heavy emergency apparatus? Is the rectangular feature adjacent to the rear lawn a swimming pool, and if so, is it currently filled with water that could serve as a suppression resource? Are there any locked or secured doors on the detached structure? Is there an address marker or reflective numbering visible from the road at the driveway entrance?
